methodology.probe_scope_note: Silver benchmark only: labels test route-level construct/scope adequacy for known GY-like needs, not a complete human relevance judgment over the catalog.

classification.authority_boundary: Catalog/Scholar search outputs remain candidate evidence until route-level semantic adequacy, scope matching, producer lineage, and consumer gates are proven.

implementation_findings.observation: HNSW index files exist, but query embedding falls back to text-only because sentence_transformers is unavailable.
Text search ranks by lexical LIKE score, but returned DatasetSearchResult.similarity is 1.0 for every text result; route consumers get no calibrated relevance threshold.
Country filtering checks coverage_countries/spatial. For four route-like probes, top topical unfiltered hits had empty countries or WORLD scope, and the country-filtered query returned zero.

silver_benchmark.label_policy: A top-k row is route-admissible only when it matches the construct and the required geography/scope. Construct-only matches are separately counted because they can still be useful candidates.

metric_binding_comparison.diagnosis: Binding layer can retrieve credit_access candidates, but search top-k was not route-admissible for Ukraine MSME.
Deterministic metric lookup exists for credit_access.
No metric binding vocabulary for firm survival/closure.
Poverty has strong metric binding coverage.
The query decomposes into energy_intensity and poverty_rate rather than a household energy-affordability construct.
Metric bindings confuse electricity access and generic average price with household electricity prices.
Displacement has strong metric binding coverage but still lacks route-level Ukraine/regional scope proof.
Cash-transfer policy instrument vocabulary is absent from metric binding search despite top-k dataset search finding cash-transfer outcome rows.

catalog_semantic_adequacy.route_verdict: Catalog search is useful as candidate discovery, but GY-1 cannot count it as admissible data discovery until construct and jurisdiction/scope adequacy are measured and consumed before FetchPlan admission.

route_like_query_probe.diagnosis: ScholarKnowledgeStore.text_search_works uses ILIKE over the whole query phrase, and embeddings are unavailable; route-like natural-language queries returned zero despite a large SKG.

web_evidence_runtime_path.g2_laundering_guard: src/polisyos/runtime/quality/proving_ground/causal_forecast_search.py rejects web_evidence_bundle_ref as L2 SKG search

knowledge_toolkit_probe.failure_mode: get_type_hints resolves annotations imported only under TYPE_CHECKING, so most methods fail registry registration at runtime.

default runtime/NL route injecting ScholarKnowledgeGraph into KnowledgeToolkit

scholar_openalex_knowledge_toolkit.route_verdict: Scholar/OpenAlex and KnowledgeToolkit are real substrate. They are not yet GY route authority for literature/prior/tool-backed search because natural-language SKG search is semantically brittle, small-business route pairs miss, web bundles are intentionally separated from L2 SKG authority, and KnowledgeToolkit tool registration is incomplete.

findings.title: Catalog top-k discovery has zero route-admissible precision on the GY-like silver benchmark
findings.summary: Across 25 top-k rows, construct-only precision was 0.56 but route-admissible construct+scope precision was 0.0. All four country-filtered cases returned zero.

findings.title: Metric binding search is stronger than free-text search but still misses policy constructs
findings.summary: credit_access, poverty_rate, displacement, and social_protection_coverage resolve; firm survival and cash transfer return zero, and energy poverty/electricity price split into weak or adjacent metric ids.

findings.title: Scholar/OpenAlex SKG is rich but route-like queries do not bridge to canonical evidence
findings.summary: Production SKG has 310,829 articles and 7,607 edges. Natural-language work search returned zero for five route-like queries; canonical edge queries work for known pairs but not small-business lending route pairs.

findings.title: KnowledgeToolkit adapter registers only 3 of 20 expected tools in a runtime probe
findings.summary: The generic adapter fails most typed methods because runtime type-hint resolution cannot see TYPE_CHECKING-only imports. Existing route uses are legal-only or formatting-only, not dataset/scholar GY search tools.

findings.title: Web evidence bundles are real but intentionally not L2 SKG authority
findings.summary: ScholarDeepSearchService can persist web evidence bundles and project them to a research DAG, and G2 guards against laundering those bundles as canonical L2 SKG search. GY-6 must choose the correct authority path instead of treating both as interchangeable literature support.

negative_assertions.reason: A topical global/WORLD/unscoped hit is a candidate, not an admissible FetchPlan source for a jurisdiction-scoped claim.
Metric binding rows still need construct, scope, source-contract, and measurement-root gates before authority.
Layer 3 G2 already rejects web_evidence_bundle_ref in canonical L2 SKG ledgers.
The adapter registered only 3 of 20 expected tools in the runtime probe, and default GY route injection was not found.

acceptance_signal_for_future_repairs: Catalog semantic benchmark has reviewed construct labels and fails closed when route_admissible_precision_at_k is below threshold.
Country/jurisdiction/scope matching is measured before FetchPlan admission, not only after retrieval.
Metric binding search and free-text dataset search share a construct handshake with DataRequirementSpec and source-contract gates.
Scholar GY route uses SKGQuery/canonical L2 rows for literature/prior authority, with query traces and no-hit frontiers persisted.
Scholar web bundles remain citation/tool evidence unless explicitly transformed into a non-L2 authority boundary.
KnowledgeToolkit adapter registers the expected typed tools under runtime imports, and one GY route run persists tool-call events and outputs.
